title: Next Greater Element IV
summary: Given a non-negative integer array, for each element, find the second greater element that meets specific conditions: there must be exactly one element between the current element and the second greater element, and the second greater element must be strictly greater than the current element.
statement: Given a non-negative integer array, for each element, find the second greater element that meets specific conditions: there must be exactly one element between the current element and the second greater element, and the second greater element must be strictly greater than the current element. If no such element exists, return -1. Return an array where each element is the second greater element found.
constraints: For each index, find the value at the second later index whose value is strictly greater than nums[i].
Return -1 where fewer than two later greater values exist.
hints: An index passes through two waiting stages as greater values arrive.
Use one decreasing stack awaiting its first greater value and another awaiting its second.
Resolve the second stack with the current value, move newly first-greater indices from the first stack to the second in order, then push the current index.
Each index changes stage exactly when a strictly greater value is encountered, so the value that removes it from the second stage is precisely its second greater value.
editorial: Each index changes stage exactly when a strictly greater value is encountered, so the value that removes it from the second stage is precisely its second greater value.

tests.explanation: For two, the greater values encountered are four then nine; analogous scans produce [9,6,6,-1,-1].
Equal values are not strictly greater, so neither index has a second greater value.
